plan.contextChunk: This figure is a heavily labeled diagram of a hyperbola opening left and right, centered at the origin of a coordinate system with arrowhead-tipped axes marked x at the right and y at the top. Two dark blue branches sweep away from the horizontal axis, one on each side. A pair of orange dashed lines cross at the center and run diagonally to the corners of the drawing, each tagged by a leader arrow reading "Asymptote" at the lower left and lower right. A teal dashed rectangle is centered on the origin, its vertical sides passing through the turning points of the two branches and its horizontal sides passing through two points on the vertical axis, with its corners sitting on the orange diagonals. A short red segment along the horizontal axis joins the two turning points and is labeled "Transverse axis" by an arrow pointing down onto it; a light blue segment along the vertical axis joins the top and bottom of the rectangle and is labeled "Conjugate axis." Dark blue dots at the ends of the red segment are each labeled "Vertex," light blue dots at the ends of the vertical segment are each labeled "Co-vertex," teal dots farther out along the horizontal axis are each labeled "Focus," and an orange marker at the crossing point is labeled "Center." Assembling every named element on one curve shows how the rectangle and its extended diagonals govern the directions the branches approach.

interactionPlan.concept: A horizontal hyperbola is completely determined by two lengths — the transverse half-axis a (where each branch turns) and the conjugate half-axis b (which sets the guide-rectangle height and hence the asymptote slope b/a) — and the dashed rectangle plus its diagonals are the construction scaffolding that encodes both.

interactions.label: Transverse half-axis a
interactions.teaches: a sets exactly where each branch turns: the vertices sit at (±a, 0), the red transverse axis spans them, and the rectangle's vertical sides move with them, so dragging a slides the turning points and re-bends the branches

interactions.label: Conjugate half-axis b
interactions.teaches: b sets the guide-rectangle height and therefore the asymptote slope b/a: increasing b steepens the orange diagonals and widens the branch opening, even though b itself never touches the curve

interactions.label: Construction guides
interactions.teaches: The dashed rectangle and asymptotes are scaffolding, not part of the hyperbola — turning them off leaves the same two branches, revealing that the guides exist only to fix the directions the branches approach

demo_steps.title: Read the anatomy
demo_steps.narration: With guides on, every named part is visible: vertices on the red transverse axis, co-vertices on the blue conjugate axis, foci outside the vertices, and the orange asymptotes running through the rectangle's corners.

demo_steps.title: Move the turning points
demo_steps.narration: Drag the transverse-axis slider: the vertices, red segment, and rectangle's vertical sides all slide together, and each branch re-bends to turn at the new (±a, 0).

demo_steps.title: Change the approach direction
demo_steps.narration: Now drag the conjugate-axis slider: the rectangle grows taller, the orange asymptotes steepen to slope b/a, and the branches open wider to follow them — b shapes the curve without ever lying on it.

demo_steps.title: Strip the scaffolding
demo_steps.narration: Toggle the guides off: the rectangle and asymptotes vanish but the two branches stay exactly where they were, confirming the guides were only the construction device encoding a and b.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: The whole hyperbola is fixed by just two numbers — a (the turning points) and b (the asymptote slope b/a) — and the dashed rectangle with its diagonals is simply the picture of those two numbers.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Centered coordinate system with arrowhead axes labeled x (right) and y (top). Two symmetric dark-blue branches opening left and right, each curving away from the x-axis and approaching the orange dashed diagonals. Teal dashed rectangle centered at origin whose vertical edges pass through the vertices and horizontal edges through the co-vertices, corners lying on the asymptotes. Red horizontal segment = transverse axis between the dark-blue vertex dots; light-blue vertical segment = conjugate axis between the light-blue co-vertex dots; teal focus dots farther out on the x-axis at (±c, 0) with c = sqrt(a^2+b^2); orange star/dot at the origin = center. Keep the figure's color coding exactly (dark blue curve, orange dashed asymptotes, teal dashed rectangle and foci, red transverse, light-blue conjugate and co-vertices). Labels use thin leader arrows as in the source. When guides toggle off, fade the rectangle and asymptotes but keep branches, dots, and axis segments; recompute asymptote slope = b/a and vertex/co-vertex/focus positions live from the two sliders.

authoredContext:
As with the ellipse, every hyperbola has two axes of symmetry. The transverse axis is a line segment that passes through the center of the hyperbola and has vertices as its endpoints. The foci lie on the line that contains the transverse axis. The conjugate axis is perpendicular to the transverse axis and has the co-vertices as its endpoints. The center of a hyperbola is the midpoint of both the transverse and conjugate axes, where they intersect. Every hyperbola also has two asymptotes that pass through its center. As a hyperbola recedes from the center, its branches approach these asymptotes. The central rectangle of the hyperbola is centered at the origin with sides that pass through each vertex and co-vertex; it is a useful tool for graphing the hyperbola and its asymptotes. To sketch the asymptotes of the hyperbola, simply sketch and extend the diagonals of the central rectangle. See the figure.

Key features of the hyperbola

This diagram illustrates the various components of a hyperbola centered at the origin, including the vertices, co-vertices, foci, transverse axis, conjugate axis, asymptotes, and the rectangular box used to construct the asymptotes.

In this section, we will limit our discussion to hyperbolas that are positioned vertically or horizontally in the coordinate plane; the axes will either lie on or be parallel to the x- and y-axes. We will consider two cases: those that are centered at the origin, and those that are centered at a point other than the origin.

discrepancies: The center is drawn as an orange filled circle with a white plus/cross, whereas the source uses an orange asterisk/star glyph at the origin.

The upper-left annotation cluster (Conjugate axis, Co-vertex) is more crowded than the source: the two leader arrows cross each other and the orange asymptote, while the source keeps them cleanly separated.
Leader arrows are generally longer and traverse more of the plot interior than the short, tight leaders in the source, adding visual clutter around the rectangle and branches.
evaluation.notes: A faithful, fully-interactive reproduction: correct horizontal hyperbola branches, dashed teal fundamental rectangle, orange dashed asymptotes through the corners, red transverse / blue conjugate axis segments, correctly placed foci/vertices/co-vertices, and all source labels with leaders; the a/b sliders, guides toggle, and 4-step player all redraw correctly and teach the right relationships (c=√(a²+b²), asymptote slope b/a). Main weaknesses are cosmetic: the center marker is a circle+cross instead of the source's star, and the upper-left leader lines crowd and cross more than in the source.
